prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from stored TokenStorage on restart never get `token_expiry_time` populated, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired access token as still valid. #1784 fixes this at the source in `_initialize()` by calling `context.update_token_expiry()` right after loading stored tokens (4-line change plus an `expired_tokens` test fixture), which lets the existing proactive-refresh check before request-send work correctly. #2875's own inline comment describes the identical root cause ("A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time... the proactive-refresh branch above is skipped") but instead patches around it by adding a new refresh-token-before-reauth branch inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401 handling. If #1784 lands, `is_token_valid()` reports the correct state up front, so the request would be proactively refreshed before ever being sent and would rarely reach the 401 branch #2875 modifies for this scenario. (2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the StreamableHTTP client's SSE reconnection logic (_handle_reconnection) ultimately fails — either by exhausting MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS or hitting an error during a reconnect attempt — the failure was never surfaced to whatever was awaiting the original in-flight request, leaving the caller hanging indefinitely instead of receiving an error. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the StreamableHTTP client's SSE reconnection logic (_handle_reconnection) ultimately fails — either by exhausting MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS or hitting an error during a reconnect attempt — the failure was never surfaced to whatever was awaiting the original in-flight request, leaving the caller hanging indefinitely instead of receiving an error. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2395's diff is self-contained and directly closes the hang: in the give-up branch of _handle_reconnection it builds a JSONRPCError (using the pending ctx.session_message.message.id) and sends it through ctx.read_stream_writer, which resolves the specific in-flight request with an error instead of leaving it stuck. This is the same error-surfacing pattern later reused by PR #3092 for non-2xx HTTP responses, keeping the failure-handling approach consistent across the file. PR #3098's diff only adds a standalone _unwrap_exception helper that walks an exception/ExceptionGroup tree to find a StreamableHTTPError; the shown diff has no visible call site wiring it to the pending request's read stream, so it addresses exception typing (e.g. for a caller wrapping the client in try/except StreamableHTTPError) without demonstrating that it resolves the specific hung request the way #2395 does.

prs.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
prs.author: Bartok9
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs change the same conditional block in validate_tool_use_result_messages that handles the case where an assistant's tool_use is not followed by a matching tool_result in the next message — but they resolve it in mutually exclusive, opposite ways. #2962 adds `has_tool_results` to the guard so the ID-matching check (and thus any error) is skipped entirely when the previous tool_use has no following tool_result at all — treating this as valid per its regression test, which cites SEP-1577 ('tool_result blocks MUST be preceded by a tool_use block, but there is NO requirement that a tool_use MUST be [followed by one]') and references originating issue #2960. #3053 leaves the outer guard unchanged but adds an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` — i.e. it still raises in that exact scenario, just with a clearer message. Applying both is impossible: one makes the case a no-op, the other makes it always an error. (2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: extract_field_from_www_auth in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py parsed the WWW-Authenticate header with naive string/regex matching, which could match a field name as a substring of another param (or split incorrectly on a comma inside a quoted value) instead of matching a complete, distinct auth-param. Both PRs fix this by adding a comma-aware tokenizer that respects quoted strings and backslash escapes before extracting fields. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: extract_field_from_www_auth in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py parsed the WWW-Authenticate header with naive string/regex matching, which could match a field name as a substring of another param (or split incorrectly on a comma inside a quoted value) instead of matching a complete, distinct auth-param. Both PRs fix this by adding a comma-aware tokenizer that respects quoted strings and backslash escapes before extracting fields. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add an escape/quote-aware comma splitter (_iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041) that are functionally equivalent. #3041 goes further by adding _extract_bearer_auth_params, which explicitly partitions each segment on the first space to isolate the scheme token and only collects params from segment(s) whose scheme is 'bearer' (case-insensitive). This handles headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Bearer ..., DPoP ...') correctly, whereas #3012's visible diff only tokenizes into a flat param list without scheme-boundary awareness, risking cross-scheme param bleed.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py unconditionally JSON-decodes any string value whose field annotation is not exactly `str`, so it corrupts valid string inputs for union-typed params (e.g. `str | None`) whenever the string happens to look like JSON (a list/object/number literal). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py unconditionally JSON-decodes any string value whose field annotation is not exactly `str`, so it corrupts valid string inputs for union-typed params (e.g. `str | None`) whenever the string happens to look like JSON (a list/object/number literal). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs change the same `field_info.annotation is not str` check in pre_parse_json, but with different scope. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` skips parsing whenever ALL union members are in a fixed `_SIMPLE_TYPES` set (str, int, float, bool, NoneType) — this also disables the previously-working JSON coercion for unions like `str | int` or `str | bool`, where decoding a numeric/boolean-looking string into its non-str member is legitimate and desired, not corruption. #2032 also checks raw membership in `_SIMPLE_TYPES` without unwrapping `Annotated[...]`, so an `Annotated`-wrapped union member (common with `Field(description=...)`) won't match the set and can fall through to a different decision than intended. #3056 targets only the exact `str | None` case its own docstring identifies as unambiguous ('no member of this union other than str could ever be produced by decoding a string as JSON'), and explicitly unwraps `Annotated[...]` via `_unwrap_annotated` before checking, so `str | Annotated[None, Field(...)]`-style params are handled correctly. #3056 is the narrower, correctness-preserving fix for the reported corruption; #2032 fixes the same case but as a side effect changes behavior for other simple-type unions it doesn't need to touch.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs change the same `field_info.annotation is not str` check in pre_parse_json, but with different scope. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` skips parsing whenever ALL union members are in a fixed `_SIMPLE_TYPES` set (str, int, float, bool, NoneType) — this also disables the previously-working JSON coercion for unions like `str | int` or `str | bool`, where decoding a numeric/boolean-looking string into its non-str member is legitimate and desired, not corruption. #2032 also checks raw membership in `_SIMPLE_TYPES` without unwrapping `Annotated[...]`, so an `Annotated`-wrapped union member (common with `Field(description=...)`) won't match the set and can fall through to a different decision than intended. #3056 targets only the exact `str | None` case its own docstring identifies as unambiguous ('no member of this union other than str could ever be produced by decoding a string as JSON'), and explicitly unwraps `Annotated[...]` via `_unwrap_annotated` before checking, so `str | Annotated[None, Field(...)]`-style params are handled correctly. #3056 is the narrower, correctness-preserving fix for the reported corruption; #2032 fixes the same case but as a side effect changes behavior for other simple-type unions it doesn't need to touch.

members.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
members.author: keurcien
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from stored TokenStorage on restart never get `token_expiry_time` populated, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired access token as still valid. #1784 fixes this at the source in `_initialize()` by calling `context.update_token_expiry()` right after loading stored tokens (4-line change plus an `expired_tokens` test fixture), which lets the existing proactive-refresh check before request-send work correctly. #2875's own inline comment describes the identical root cause ("A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time... the proactive-refresh branch above is skipped") but instead patches around it by adding a new refresh-token-before-reauth branch inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401 handling. If #1784 lands, `is_token_valid()` reports the correct state up front, so the request would be proactively refreshed before ever being sent and would rarely reach the 401 branch #2875 modifies for this scenario. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs change the same `field_info.annotation is not str` check in pre_parse_json, but with different scope. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` skips parsing whenever ALL union members are in a fixed `_SIMPLE_TYPES` set (str, int, float, bool, NoneType) — this also disables the previously-working JSON coercion for unions like `str | int` or `str | bool`, where decoding a numeric/boolean-looking string into its non-str member is legitimate and desired, not corruption. #2032 also checks raw membership in `_SIMPLE_TYPES` without unwrapping `Annotated[...]`, so an `Annotated`-wrapped union member (common with `Field(description=...)`) won't match the set and can fall through to a different decision than intended. #3056 targets only the exact `str | None` case its own docstring identifies as unambiguous ('no member of this union other than str could ever be produced by decoding a string as JSON'), and explicitly unwraps `Annotated[...]` via `_unwrap_annotated` before checking, so `str | Annotated[None, Field(...)]`-style params are handled correctly. #3056 is the narrower, correctness-preserving fix for the reported corruption; #2032 fixes the same case but as a side effect changes behavior for other simple-type unions it doesn't need to touch.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2395's diff is self-contained and directly closes the hang: in the give-up branch of _handle_reconnection it builds a JSONRPCError (using the pending ctx.session_message.message.id) and sends it through ctx.read_stream_writer, which resolves the specific in-flight request with an error instead of leaving it stuck. This is the same error-surfacing pattern later reused by PR #3092 for non-2xx HTTP responses, keeping the failure-handling approach consistent across the file. PR #3098's diff only adds a standalone _unwrap_exception helper that walks an exception/ExceptionGroup tree to find a StreamableHTTPError; the shown diff has no visible call site wiring it to the pending request's read stream, so it addresses exception typing (e.g. for a caller wrapping the client in try/except StreamableHTTPError) without demonstrating that it resolves the specific hung request the way #2395 does.

members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs change the same conditional block in validate_tool_use_result_messages that handles the case where an assistant's tool_use is not followed by a matching tool_result in the next message — but they resolve it in mutually exclusive, opposite ways. #2962 adds `has_tool_results` to the guard so the ID-matching check (and thus any error) is skipped entirely when the previous tool_use has no following tool_result at all — treating this as valid per its regression test, which cites SEP-1577 ('tool_result blocks MUST be preceded by a tool_use block, but there is NO requirement that a tool_use MUST be [followed by one]') and references originating issue #2960. #3053 leaves the outer guard unchanged but adds an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` — i.e. it still raises in that exact scenario, just with a clearer message. Applying both is impossible: one makes the case a no-op, the other makes it always an error. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both add an escape/quote-aware comma splitter (_iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041) that are functionally equivalent. #3041 goes further by adding _extract_bearer_auth_params, which explicitly partitions each segment on the first space to isolate the scheme token and only collects params from segment(s) whose scheme is 'bearer' (case-insensitive). This handles headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Bearer ..., DPoP ...') correctly, whereas #3012's visible diff only tokenizes into a flat param list without scheme-boundary awareness, risking cross-scheme param bleed.
